Title: Your island adventure reaches the Galápagos. Which country are you visiting?
AnswerDetails: The Galápagos belong to Ecuador, roughly 1,000 km from its mainland. This is a real offshore adventure, not a quick bridge crossing!

Title: Umbrella-shaped dragon’s blood trees give which Yemeni archipelago its otherworldly look?
AnswerDetails: Socotra is home to the remarkable dragon’s blood tree. The silhouette looks borrowed from science fiction, but the tree is entirely real.

Title: Which island’s monumental stone figures are called moai?
AnswerDetails: The moai are monumental sculptures of Rapa Nui, also known as Easter Island. They are cultural works created by people, not mysterious visitors from space.

Title: Surtsey appeared above the sea in 1963. Which country gained this new volcanic island?
AnswerDetails: Surtsey emerged during an eruption off Iceland. In this case, the landscape really did get a new addition within living memory.

Title: To visit the islands of Komodo National Park, which country goes on your itinerary?
AnswerDetails: Komodo National Park is in Indonesia. Its rugged islands and surrounding marine waters make this much more than a single-animal destination.

Title: Aldabra Atoll belongs to Seychelles. Which ocean surrounds it?
AnswerDetails: Aldabra lies in the Indian Ocean. Its raised coral landscape is a reminder that tiny-looking islands can have enormous natural importance.

Title: At very high tides, which French landmark becomes an island again?
AnswerDetails: High tides can surround Mont-Saint-Michel with water. The sea gets to redraw the access map, so this is definitely a place to respect tide guidance.

Title: The Rainforests of the Atsinanana run along the eastern side of which island?
AnswerDetails: These forests occupy parts of eastern Madagascar. The unfamiliar name is a good excuse to look beyond the usual beach-island postcard.

Title: Kinabalu Park is in Malaysian Sabah, on which large island?
AnswerDetails: Kinabalu Park sits at the northern end of Borneo. An island trip can mean mountain scenery rather than a deckchair.

Title: Sigiriya’s spectacular Lion Rock is a landmark of which island country?
AnswerDetails: Sigiriya is in Sri Lanka, with ancient remains around and atop its dramatic rock. The entrance’s lion imagery makes the name especially memorable.

Title: Which ocean basin is so vast that its area exceeds that of all the continents combined?
AnswerDetails: The Pacific is that enormous. On a globe turned the right way, Earth makes an excellent case for the nickname water planet.

Title: Which of the five commonly named ocean basins is the smallest?
AnswerDetails: The Arctic is the smallest of the five commonly named ocean basins. Smallest is relative: this is still an ocean, not a chilly pond.

Title: Which sea is bounded by ocean currents rather than land?
AnswerDetails: Currents define the Sargasso Sea’s boundaries. It breaks the familiar mental picture of a sea tucked between coastlines.

Title: Which river supplies the thunderous water at Victoria Falls?
AnswerDetails: Victoria Falls interrupts the Zambezi River. All that spectacular spray begins as a river continuing its journey.

Title: Iguazú Falls stretches across the border of which pair of countries?
AnswerDetails: The falls span Argentina and Brazil. One magnificent waterfall system gives visitors two national perspectives.

Title: The Okavango Delta is an inland watery wonder in which country?
AnswerDetails: The Okavango Delta lies in northwestern Botswana. Its inland setting is the twist: a delta does not have to sit at an ocean coastline.

Title: Which strait separates Alaska from northeastern Siberia?
AnswerDetails: The Bering Strait separates Alaska and Siberia. It links the Bering Sea with the Chukchi Sea, giving it a big job between two ocean regions.

Title: A semi-enclosed coastal water body where a freshwater river meets the sea is called what?
AnswerDetails: That meeting place is an estuary. Think of it as a watery transition zone, rather than a hard line where river suddenly becomes ocean.

Title: From above, a coral reef forms a ring around a lagoon. What are you looking at?
AnswerDetails: An atoll is a ring-like coral reef enclosing a lagoon. The aerial view really does help the geography click.

Title: Roughly how much of Earth’s surface is covered by the ocean?
AnswerDetails: The ocean covers about 71 percent of Earth’s surface. Our land-focused maps can make it easy to forget which side wins the area contest.

Title: Most of Yellowstone National Park lies in which U.S. state?
AnswerDetails: About 96 percent of Yellowstone lies in Wyoming. Montana and Idaho share the park too, so the state line is not the park boundary.

Title: Kilimanjaro’s summit rises in which country?
AnswerDetails: Kilimanjaro is in Tanzania. Its 5,895-metre summit makes it an unmistakable feature of the African landscape.

Title: The dramatic sea towers of Ha Long Bay are made mainly of which rock?
AnswerDetails: Ha Long Bay’s islands and islets are limestone. Nature has turned rock and water into a skyline without a single skyscraper.

Title: The Giant’s Causeway’s interlocking columns are made of which volcanic rock?
AnswerDetails: The columns are basalt, associated with ancient volcanic activity. They can look designed, but geology did the construction.

Title: Pamukkale’s name is commonly translated as what?
AnswerDetails: Pamukkale means Cotton Palace. Its pale mineral terraces explain the nickname far better than any actual cotton crop could.

Title: What mineral gives White Sands National Park its unusual pale dunes?
AnswerDetails: White Sands is famous for gypsum sand. Sand describes grain size, not one compulsory mineral recipe.

Title: Wadi Rum’s dramatic desert landscape is in which country?
AnswerDetails: Wadi Rum is in southern Jordan. Its desert setting shows how a landscape can be visually rich without being green.

Title: Te Wāhipounamu’s mountains and fiords occupy which part of New Zealand?
AnswerDetails: Te Wāhipounamu lies in the southwest of the South Island. Mountains, glaciers, forests and fiords pack an impressive variety into this region.

Title: Crater Lake sits on the crest of the Cascades in which U.S. state?
AnswerDetails: Crater Lake is in southern Oregon. The deep blue water occupies a volcanic landscape rather than a crater punched out by a space rock.

Title: Which river runs through the Grand Canyon?
AnswerDetails: The Colorado River runs through the Grand Canyon and played the central role in carving it. Water can be a very patient sculptor.

Title: Which Italian city spreads across 118 small islands in a lagoon?
AnswerDetails: Venice’s historic city spreads across 118 small islands. Here, water is part of the street-plan story, not just the scenery.

Title: Machu Picchu stands where the Peruvian Andes meet the edge of which great basin?
AnswerDetails: Machu Picchu occupies the meeting zone of the Andes and Amazon Basin. Its setting is a mountain-and-forest story as well as an architectural one.

Title: Petra, the ancient city famous for rock-cut monuments, is in which country?
AnswerDetails: Petra is in Jordan. It is a city where the rock is part of the architecture, not merely the ground underneath it.

Title: You are exploring the historic medina of Fez. Which country are you in?
AnswerDetails: Fez is in Morocco. Its historic medina preserves a distinctive urban landscape shaped over many centuries.

Title: Timbuktu is a real city, not just a phrase for far away. In which country is it?
AnswerDetails: Timbuktu is in Mali. A place that often gets used as shorthand for remoteness deserves its own real pin on the map.

Title: Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur are the three ancient cities of a valley in which country?
AnswerDetails: They are in Nepal’s Kathmandu Valley. The valley brings three historic city stories into one geographical setting.

Title: The Aztec city beneath modern Mexico City began on an island in which lake?
AnswerDetails: Tenochtitlan was founded on an island in Lake Texcoco. Modern Mexico City has a watery origin that its streets do not immediately advertise.

Title: Which planned capital’s design is associated with Lúcio Costa and architect Oscar Niemeyer?
AnswerDetails: Brasília combines Costa’s city plan with Niemeyer’s architecture. In this capital, the layout itself is part of the landmark.

Title: Istanbul’s famous setting sits at the meeting of which two continents?
AnswerDetails: Istanbul is associated with the meeting of Europe and Asia around the Bosphorus. This is a city whose location helps explain its long historical importance.

Title: Which river is central to Cairo’s geography and history?
AnswerDetails: The Nile is central to Cairo’s story. The city’s ports, canals and water infrastructure show how geography shapes urban life.

Title: Which imaginary line is assigned latitude 0°?
AnswerDetails: The equator is latitude 0°. It provides the starting line for measuring how far north or south a place lies.

Title: A map pin reads 25° S. What does that tell you?
AnswerDetails: The S means south latitude, measured from the equator. It tells you a hemisphere, not the country or the kind of landscape.
OptionA: It is 25 km from a pole
OptionB: It is south of the equator
OptionC: It is south of the prime meridian
OptionD: It is in the Southern Ocean

Title: Which named line lies at roughly 23.5° north latitude?
AnswerDetails: The Tropic of Cancer lies about 23.5° north. Capricorn is its southern counterpart, so the two tropical names are not interchangeable.

Title: Unlike parallel latitude lines, lines of longitude meet where?
AnswerDetails: Lines of longitude converge at the poles. A flat map can hide that globe-shaped detail.

Title: The antimeridian opposite 0° longitude has what longitude?
AnswerDetails: The antimeridian is at 180° longitude. It supplies the broad geographical basis for the International Date Line, though that boundary does not follow it perfectly.

Title: The International Date Line runs mainly through which ocean?
AnswerDetails: The date line runs mainly through the Pacific. Its bends remind us that calendar boundaries are human arrangements laid over geography.

Title: On a topographic map, a contour line joins points with the same what?
AnswerDetails: Contour lines connect equal elevations. They let a flat sheet of paper describe a very un-flat landscape.

Title: Your hiking map’s contour lines suddenly crowd together. What lies ahead?
AnswerDetails: Closely spaced contour lines indicate a steep slope. Your map is politely warning your legs before the climb begins.

Title: On a USGS topographic map, a blue dashed-and-dotted stream line indicates what?
AnswerDetails: USGS uses a dashed-and-dotted blue line for an intermittent stream. That is different from the solid blue line used for a perennial stream.

Title: On a map scaled 1:24,000, one inch represents how many feet on the ground?
AnswerDetails: One map inch represents 24,000 real inches, which is 2,000 feet. A tiny ruler measurement can stand for a surprisingly long walk.

Title: Which moving natural force typically scours a valley into a broad U-shape?
AnswerDetails: Glaciers can widen and steepen valleys into a U-shape. A glacier is not just frozen scenery: it is a slow-moving landscape tool.

Title: A long, narrow sea inlet in a steep-sided glacial valley is called what?
AnswerDetails: That sea-filled glacial valley is a fjord. It is a watery clue to the ice that once shaped the coast.

Title: In a rain shadow, which side of a mountain range tends to receive less precipitation?
AnswerDetails: The leeward side tends to be drier. Mountains can change the weather story dramatically over a surprisingly short map distance.

Title: Hawaiian volcanoes are classic examples of volcanism above what?
AnswerDetails: Hawaii is a classic hotspot example within a plate. Not every volcano needs to sit on a plate boundary.
OptionA: A boundary where two plates slide past each other
OptionB: A subduction zone at a plate edge
OptionC: A hotspot beneath a tectonic plate

Title: The volcanic belt nicknamed the Ring of Fire surrounds which ocean?
AnswerDetails: The Ring of Fire encircles the Pacific region. The name describes a broad belt of volcanic activity, not a literal burning ring.

Title: Crater Lake’s basin formed chiefly when Mount Mazama did what?
AnswerDetails: Mount Mazama erupted and collapsed, producing a caldera that later held the lake. The word crater can tempt you toward the wrong space-impact story.
OptionC: Was pulled apart along a rift valley

Title: What deposited the pale terraces at Pamukkale?
AnswerDetails: Mineral-rich spring water built Pamukkale’s terraces. The snowy appearance is a visual trick: the white landscape is mineral, not a permanent snowdrift.

Title: In the classic explanation of atoll formation, what happens to the central volcanic island while the reef keeps growing?
AnswerDetails: The island gradually subsides while coral growth can maintain a reef around it. Over geological time, a ring and lagoon can remain where an island once stood.
OptionA: It remains fixed while the lagoon drains
OptionC: It rises while the reef retreats
OptionD: It grows outward until it covers the reef

Title: What natural processes break White Sands’ gypsum crystals into smaller sand grains?
AnswerDetails: Wind and water break the crystals into smaller particles. Those brilliant dunes begin with minerals being worked down to sand-sized grains.

Title: Spring tides are associated with which arrangement of the Sun, Moon and Earth?
AnswerDetails: Spring tides occur around new and full moons, when the three are roughly aligned. Spring here is about the tidal range, not the season.
OptionA: Sun and Moon at their greatest distances from Earth
OptionB: Sun and Moon at right angles as seen from Earth
OptionD: Sun and Moon at their closest distances to Earth
